articles.title: The world once again calls for an end to the US blockade on Cuba
articles.author: Pablo Meriguet
articles.content_excerpt: Last Wednesday, October 28, the United Nations General Assembly voted (for the thirty-fourth time) in favor of ending the economic and commercial embargo – which many refer to as a blockade – that the United States has unilaterally imposed on Cuba for more than sixty years. With 130 votes in favor, 17 against, and 25 abstentions, the international community once again demanded that the United States end an embargo that has caused unimaginable hardship for the Cuban people and has slowed the Caribbean nation’s development. One of the countries that voted against the embargo was South Africa, whose ambassador emphasized his concern about the negative consequences the Cuban people are suffering as a result of Washington’s decisions. articles.title: Thousands of farmers march for land rights in India’s Maharashtra
articles.author: Abdul Rahman
articles.content_excerpt: Earlier this week, thousands of farmers in India’s western state of Maharashtra marched to its capital, Mumbai, and forced the state government to recognize their right to the land they have tilled for years and fulfill their demands. Over 12,000 in number, the farmers, carrying red flags and shouting slogans against the ultra-right-wing government led by the Hindu-supremacist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), were led by the All India Kisan Sabha (AIKS), a left-wing farmers’ union. The farmers were also supported by several other left-wing mass organizations, such as the Center for Indian Trade Unions (CITU) and Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI). articles.title: ICE arrests of Dominicans in Puerto Rico spark outrage and reignite calls for independence
articles.author: Devin B. Martinez
articles.content_excerpt: Masked Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents carrying long guns swept through working-class neighborhoods in San Juan, Puerto Rico between October 22-25. About a dozen workers, largely Dominican immigrants, were reportedly detained from Río Piedras, Capetillo, Villa Palmeras, Villa Capri, and Barrio Obrero. Local leaders and community members have expressed outrage over the ICE deployment to the island. Protests have also broken out, demanding ICE out of Puerto Rico and elevating calls for independence from the United States. During the operations, federal agents claimed that they were detaining criminals, but locals say they were all hard working people, many with families. articles.title: How did Lula win the election?
articles.author: Pablo Meriguet
articles.content_excerpt: On October 25, Brazil’s three-time and current president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, surprised the entire world by overcoming an electoral setback in the first round (in which he was defeated by the far-right candidate Flávio Bolsonaro) and securing victory and the presidential seat in Brasília. Lula, the legendary union leader during the dictatorship, secured 51.79%, equivalent to 64,256,232 votes, while Bolsonaro (son of the detained former president Jair Bolsonaro) received 48.21%, or 59,826,041 votes.
